title: Graceful standby promotion and rolling KV reconciliation experiment
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Goal: run a controlled active->passive switchover experiment that promotes a warm standby region with zero-downtime intent by using a rolling KV reconciliation window and phased traffic siphon. This ticket captures the playbook, validation harness, automation hooks, and post-mortem checklist. Motivation: previous drills showed brief cache divergence and token-store race windows during quick switchover; the proposed approach trades a small promotion lag for strong data integrity guarantees and predictable SLO adherence.
playbook_steps: Pre-run: confirm backup snapshot completeness (S3 manifest checksum + object counts) and recent incremental snapshot applied to standby; blocklist long-running migrations; notify on-call + stakeholders; set drill window in PagerDuty

Pre-run: assert health of regional infra (GPU pools, tokenstore replicas, leader election status) via /infra/health and clean alerts in Grafana: dashboards/runtime-overview and dashboards/tokenstore-replication

Snapshot: take a final consistent snapshot of primary tokenstore and KV-blobstore; run snap-verify script that validates checksums and sample key counts (sha256 aggregation); store to s3://redwood-dr-snapshots/2026-02-XX
Quarantine: place primary in read-only warm-quarantine mode (accepts reads, rejects writes) and enable 'golden-gate' ingress filter so new writes are redirected to a staging queue for reconciliation

Progressive KV reconciliation: start rolling reconciliation process on standby in windowed batches (key ranges sharded by prefix). For each shard: apply idempotent reconcile operations, run sampling verification, and mark shard healthy. Use max parallelism of 8 to limit CPU/GPU impact
Traffic siphon phase 0 (0%): run synthetic SLO probes from control-plane to standby only, verify p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput against target SLOs for 15 minutes
Circuit-breaker calibration: set temporary circuit thresholds on frontend routers: p99=750ms, error-rate=0.5% for auto-fallback. Ensure breaker-propagation across edge proxies and SDK clients

Traffic siphon phase 1 (10%): route 10% of new session requests to standby via smart-routing policy; monitor KV-read-miss rate, cache warm-up, and latency. Abort if KV divergence > 0.01% or SLOs violated for >2 minutes
Traffic siphon phase 2 (50%): after 30m of stable metrics, increase to 50% with canary fencing (auto-rollback hooks). Continue reconciliation and scale up cache warmers as necessary

Final promotion (time-bound): once reconciliation status shows 100% shard healthy and synthetic SLO probes pass for 45m, flip primary DNS/policy to promote standby to active. Keep old primary in read-only mode for 2 hours as shadow store
Post-promotion validation: run full restore-verify suite (integrity, sample-query equivalence, end-to-end generation quality tests using seeded prompts), collect traces for 24 hours

Rollback: if at any step thresholds are violated (SLO breach, reconciliation failure, or circuit events), execute automatic rollback: reduce traffic to standby to 0%, re-enable writes on primary, and run a detailed diff to reconcile any queued writes
Post-run audit: produce audit diff for tokenstore and KV write streams, store artifacts, and create follow-up tickets for observed gaps
success_criteria: No more than 1 minute of elevated error rate (>1%) at any tier during the run
Synthetic SLO probes show p99 <= 750ms and error-rate < 0.5% for 45 consecutive minutes prior to final promotion
KV reconciliation completes with <0.001% unresolved keys; unresolved keys must be triaged with a manual remediation plan
Automatic rollback hooks executed and validated in <5 minutes if triggered
Post-run restore-verify passes with data-integrity checksum matching between primary and promoted standby
validation_checks: snap-verify output: checksum parity + sampled key counts
kv-reconcile-meter: per-shard success/failure rates and end-to-end applied operations
synthetic-probes: latency distribution and token-accuracy regression tests stored in metrics.vectors
circuit-breaker logs: number of tripped events and duration
audit-diff: top-100 inconsistent keys with root-cause tags
billing throttle watch: ensure cost anomaly detection doesn't trigger unexpected autoscaling
